title: Hyperspace  More Nodes Is All You Need: Nicolas Schlaepfer
talk_summary: A short product pitch for Hyperspace, a decentralized inference network plus a node-editor agent builder that turns a query into a DAG plan, streams editable nodes, and executes each node with a reasoning model plus a summarization model. It is mostly a demo of primitives (DAG planning, Puppeteer/BeautifulSoup scraping to markdown, python execution, virtual filesystem) rather than measured engineering results.

takeaways.what_they_do: A fine-tuned model emits a methodical plan as a JSON DAG; each node is streamed into an editor where the user can edit title, task description, and expected output, or add nodes before execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you put in a query you get in a dag or you get out a dag in a Json format

takeaways.technique: Per-node prompt assembled from global goal + local goal + prior node output
takeaways.what_they_do: Each node builds its own query by combining the overall goal, the node's local goal, and whatever happened in the previous node, keeping per-call context scoped to the node.

takeaways.technique: Split reasoning vs summarization models per node
takeaways.what_they_do: They route reasoning to one model (Qwen 2 instruct) and summarization to another (Llama 3 70B) so outputs are synthesized from diverse models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for reasoning we're using quen 2 instruct and then for summarization we're using llama 370b

takeaways.what_they_do: They scrape with Puppeteer and BeautifulSoup and convert HTML to markdown before feeding it to the LLM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: scrape websites convert that uh HTML into uh a markdown something easier to read for llms to digest

takeaways.what_they_do: Execution is gated on a reviewable node graph the user can modify, add to, or re-title before running.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to emphasize that the user still in full control they can edit the title task description and expected output
